steps.name: basics
steps.label: Basics
steps.description: M365Permissions runs in your own Azure subscription and shows who can reach what in Microsoft 365, Entra ID and Azure. A few minutes after the deployment, we mail you a page that follows the installation. The instance then shows the setup command a Global Administrator runs. If a policy requires tags on resource groups, create the resource group with its tags first and choose it here, and tag the managed application on the Tags step: its managed resource group takes those tags.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Where you'll run it and keep data. A network you peer with may be in another region (Azure then charges for the traffic between regions).

elements.name: plan
elements.label: Plan
elements.toolTip: Standard and Enterprise scan the same; Enterprise adds support. See m365permissions.com.

elements.name: welcomeMail
elements.label: Your mail address
elements.toolTip: The main contact for this instance. JSolve sends the installation page, update information and support messages there. You can change it later in M365Permissions under Settings, Contact.

elements.name: tenantName
elements.label: Organisation name
elements.toolTip: Shown in M365Permissions on reports, optional.

elements.name: planSku
elements.label: Size
elements.toolTip: Choose by your number of users. This is the minimum size: the plan never moves below it. The smallest size starts one size up until the first scan is done, and moves up again while a large scan backlog lasts.

options.text: The instance's resources are protected, its managed identity looks after them (updates etc). People sign in to M365Permissions with their Entra ID account; the setup command makes you Admin.

elements.name: alertSenderMailbox
elements.label: Mailbox for alert mails (optional)
elements.toolTip: A mailbox in your tenant that M365Permissions may send alerts from (a shared mailbox is enough). The setup command lets M365Permissions send ONLY from that mailbox (vs Mail.Send graph permissions). Empty: no alert mails.

options.text: M365Permissions runs in its own virtual network, and its storage and Key Vault accept connections from that network only. Choose a range that does not overlap your networks if you may connect it later.

elements.name: addressSpace
elements.label: Address space for the instance (CIDR, /20 to /25)
elements.toolTip: A free range that does not overlap your networks or their peers, for example 10.250.0.0/24. The instance uses two /26 subnets of it.

constraints.validationMessage: An IPv4 range in CIDR form, /20 to /25.

elements.name: dataAccess
elements.label: Storage and Key Vault reached through
elements.toolTip: Service endpoints: storage and Key Vault keep a public address, but their firewall only allows the web app. Private endpoints: they get a private address in the instance's network and no public address at all; three private endpoints cost about USD 0.82 a day.

elements.name: access
elements.label: How to secure M365Permissions
elements.toolTip: Allowed IP ranges only: internet routed, your organisation's addresses. Peering: the instance peers with a virtual network of yours and gets a private endpoint. Your own private endpoint: you create a private endpoint after install, to M365Permissions in a network of yours (hub or spoke, any subscription); no peering.

options.text: The instance gets a private endpoint and peers with your chosen network, in any subscription you can see and any region (across regions Azure charges for the traffic). The setup command gives the instance's scan identity Network Contributor on your network only; the instance then makes both peering links (its own allows forwarded traffic, so your spokes can come through a firewall in your hub) and links its private DNS zone (privatelink.azurewebsites.net) to your network, or keeps its records in your own zone. Without allowed IP ranges only its setup page is reachable from the internet until then, so the setup command can be fetched: nobody can sign in and nothing is scanned. It then closes itself to the internet, so it opens only from your network. With allowed IP ranges it stays reachable from those ranges and your network, also during setup: run the setup command from inside the ranges. With custom DNS servers, forward azurewebsites.net to Azure DNS (168.63.129.16).

No peering and no DNS zone of the instance's: once it runs, create a private endpoint to its web app (sub-resource sites) in a network of yours, with manual approval. Its connection waits until an Admin approves it in M365Permissions under Settings, Access, because anyone could ask for one. M365Permissions then closes itself to the internet, unless allowed IP ranges keep it reachable. Allowed IP ranges are required: they are the way in until the first approval. Your DNS (a central privatelink.azurewebsites.net zone, or a policy) holds the record, or name your zone below and the instance keeps its records there.

elements.name: virtualNetwork
elements.label: Your virtual network
elements.toolTip: The network to peer with: a hub or a spoke, in any subscription you can see and any region.

elements.name: outbound
elements.label: Outbound traffic
elements.toolTip: How M365Permissions reaches Microsoft 365, Azure and JSolve. Through your network: a firewall you name, or the default route your hub already advertises. Either way Azure Resource Manager stays direct, so M365Permissions can always switch back. An Admin changes it later under Settings, Access.

allowedValues.label: Through a firewall in that network
Through the routes my hub advertises

elements.name: firewallIp
elements.label: Private IP address of your firewall
elements.toolTip: The firewall (or other network virtual appliance) in the network you peer with, for example 10.0.1.4. Peering passes nothing on to other networks, so it must be in that one.

constraints.validationMessage: A private IPv4 address, for example 10.0.1.4.

options.text: Once the peering is up, M365Permissions sends everything except Azure Resource Manager to this address, tests sign-in and Microsoft Graph through it and goes back to direct traffic by itself when they cannot be reached within 3 minutes. Your firewall has to allow what M365Permissions reaches: Microsoft 365, Azure, Power BI and JSolve.

For a hub with a VPN or ExpressRoute gateway or Azure Route Server that advertises a default route (0.0.0.0/0). Once the peering is up, the instance's side of the peering uses your hub's gateway and your side allows gateway transit (the instance sets that with the Network Contributor role the setup command gives it). M365Permissions then checks that the default route arrived and that sign-in and Microsoft Graph are reached, and goes back to direct traffic by itself when not, within 3 minutes. Azure Resource Manager stays direct.

elements.name: useZone
elements.label: Use my existing private DNS zone
elements.toolTip: For hub-spoke networks with a central privatelink.azurewebsites.net zone: a network links to only one zone of that name. The instance then makes no zone of its own; the setup command gives its scan identity Private DNS Zone Contributor on that zone only, and the instance keeps its two A records (the web app and its scm name) there, and no others.

elements.name: privateDnsZone
elements.label: Resource id of your privatelink.azurewebsites.net zone
elements.toolTip: In the Azure portal: the private DNS zone, Properties (or JSON View), Resource ID. Any subscription of this tenant.

constraints.validationMessage: The resource id of a private DNS zone named privatelink.azurewebsites.net.

elements.name: allowedIpRanges
elements.label: Allowed IP ranges (required unless peered with your virtual network)
elements.toolTip: Public IPv4 addresses or ranges (CIDR), comma separated, for example 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.7. Only these can open M365Permissions from the internet, until you change them inside M365Permissions under Settings, Access; include the address the Global Administrator runs the setup command from. M365Permissions is never open to everyone: without peering at least one is required (with your own private endpoint until its first approval), with peering an empty list means it opens only from your network.

constraints.validationMessage: IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges of /8 or narrower, comma separated. Required unless M365Permissions is peered with your virtual network.

elements.name: tagsByResource
elements.toolTip: Tags on the managed application also go on its managed resource group.

options.text: With just-in-time access on, support can modify the application only for a time you approve, for example to repair a broken deployment. It starts with automatic approval for up to 8 hours; change that on the managed application's JIT Configuration page. It can only be switched on now. Without it support always has access. No additional cost.

elements.name: jitEnabled
elements.label: Just-in-time access
elements.toolTip: Support reaches the resources only after a request you approve (automatically at first).
